sentences.text: The holotype specimen includes parts of the skull and lower jaws.
This skeleton is missing the tail and most of the foot bones.
A distinctive feature is the jugal bone, which has a high front branch ending in a sharp, needle-like point.
The shoulder blade is fan-like expanded toward the rear.
The pteroid bone is small and slender, shaped like an exclamation mark.
The fossil represents a subadult individual that was not fully grown.
Amateur paleontologist Umberto Venier discovered the holotype skeleton in 1997 in a boulder in the Seazza brook near Preone in the Dolomites.
The genus and its type species, Seazzadactylus venieri, were formally named and described by Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia in 2019.
The generic name Seazzadactylus combines the name of the Seazza brook with the Greek word for 'finger'.
The specific name venieri honors Umberto Venier as the discoverer of the fossil.
Seazzadactylus is classified as a basal pterosaur outside of the Monofenestrata clade.
Cladistic analysis places Seazzadactylus in a clade with Arcticodactylus, Austriadraco, Carniadactylus, Raeticodactylus, and Caviramus.
The clade containing Seazzadactylus was named Caviramidae in a 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron.
In the evolutionary tree, Seazzadactylus is positioned directly above Austriadraco and below Carniadactylus.
Seazzadactylus is classified within the unranked family Eopterosauria.
Seazzadactylus lived during the late Triassic, specifically the Norian stage between 219 and 214 million years ago, in what is now Italy.
The time range for Seazzadactylus is recorded as the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
